title_en: Basic Law of the Macao Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 The Macao Special Administrative Region is an inalienable part of the People's Republic of China.

Article 2 The National People's Congress of the People's Republic of China authorizes the Macao Special Administrative Region to exercise a high degree of autonomy in accordance with the provisions of this Law, and to enjoy executive power, legislative power, independent judicial power and the power of final adjudication.

Article 3 The executive authorities and the legislature of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall be composed of permanent residents of the Macao Special Administrative Region in accordance with the relevant provisions of this Law.
Article 4 The Macao Special Administrative Region shall safeguard the rights and freedoms of residents of the Macao Special Administrative Region and other persons in accordance with law.

Article 5 The Macao Special Administrative Region shall not practice the socialist system or policies, and shall maintain the existing capitalist system and way of life for fifty years without change.
Article 6 The Macao Special Administrative Region shall protect private property rights by law.

Article 7 The land and natural resources within the Macao Special Administrative Region shall be owned by the State, except for private land that has been legally confirmed prior to the establishment of the Macao Special Administrative Region. The Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall be responsible for the administration, use, development, lease or grant of such land and resources to individuals or legal persons for use or development, and the revenue derived therefrom shall be entirely at the disposal of the Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region.

Article 8 The laws, decrees, administrative regulations and other normative documents previously in force in Macao shall be maintained, except for those that contravene this Law or those that have been amended by the legislature or other relevant organs of the Macao Special Administrative Region in accordance with legal procedures.

Article 9 In addition to the Chinese language, the Portuguese language may also be used by the executive authorities, legislature and judicial organs of the Macao Special Administrative Region. The Portuguese language shall also be an official language.

Article 10 In addition to displaying and using the national flag and national emblem of the People's Republic of China, the Macao Special Administrative Region may display and use its own regional flag and regional emblem. The regional flag of the Macao Special Administrative Region is a green flag with five stars, a lotus flower, a bridge and sea water. The regional emblem of the Macao Special Administrative Region consists of five stars, a lotus flower, a bridge and sea water in the center, surrounded by the words 'Macao Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China' in Chinese and 'Macau' in Portuguese.

Article 11 In accordance with Article 31 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of China, the systems and policies of the Macao Special Administrative Region, including the social and economic systems, the systems for safeguarding the fundamental rights and freedoms of residents, the systems of executive, legislative and judicial administration, as well as related policies, shall be based on the provisions of this Law. No law, decree, administrative regulation or other normative document enacted by the Macao Special Administrative Region may contravene this Law.

Article 12 The Macao Special Administrative Region is a local administrative region of the People's Republic of China that enjoys a high degree of autonomy and comes directly under the Central People's Government.

Article 13 The Central People's Government shall be responsible for foreign affairs relating to the Macao Special Administrative Region. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China shall establish an office in Macao to handle foreign affairs. The Central People's Government authorizes the Macao Special Administrative Region to conduct relevant external affairs on its own in accordance with this Law.

Article 14 The Central People's Government shall be responsible for the defense of the Macao Special Administrative Region. The Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall be responsible for maintaining public order in the Macao Special Administrative Region.

Article 15 The Central People's Government shall appoint and remove the Chief Executive, principal officials of the government and the Procurator-General of the Macao Special Administrative Region in accordance with the relevant provisions of this Law.

Article 16 The Macao Special Administrative Region shall enjoy executive power, and shall on its own handle administrative affairs of the Macao Special Administrative Region in accordance with the relevant provisions of this Law.

Article 17 The Macao Special Administrative Region shall enjoy legislative power. Laws enacted by the legislature of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall be reported to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for the record. The act of reporting for the record shall not affect the coming into force of such laws. If the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, after consulting the Committee for the Basic Law of the Macao Special Administrative Region under it, considers that any law enacted by the legislature of the Macao Special Administrative Region is not consistent with the provisions of this Law regarding affairs within the responsibility of the Central Authorities or regarding the relationship between the Central Authorities and the Macao Special Administrative Region, it may return the law in question, but shall not amend it. Any law returned by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall immediately cease to have effect. Such cessation of effect shall have no retroactive effect, unless otherwise provided for by the laws of the Macao Special Administrative Region.

Article 18 The laws in force in the Macao Special Administrative Region shall be this Law, the laws previously in force in Macao as provided for in Article 8 of this Law, and the laws enacted by the legislature of the Macao Special Administrative Region. National laws shall not be applied in the Macao Special Administrative Region, except for those listed in Annex III to this Law. Laws listed in Annex III to this Law shall be applied locally by the Macao Special Administrative Region through promulgation or legislation. The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress may, after consulting the Committee for the Basic Law of the Macao Special Administrative Region under it and the Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region, add to or delete from the list of laws in Annex III to this Law. Laws listed in Annex III shall be confined to those relating to national defense, foreign affairs and other matters that are not within the autonomy of the Macao Special Administrative Region in accordance with this Law. In the event that the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress decides to declare a state of war or, by reason of turmoil within the Macao Special Administrative Region which endangers national unity or security and is beyond the control of the Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region, decides that the Macao Special Administrative Region is in a state of emergency, the Central People's Government may issue an order applying the relevant national laws in the Macao Special Administrative Region.

Article 19 The Macao Special Administrative Region shall enjoy independent judicial power and the power of final adjudication. The courts of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall have jurisdiction over all cases in the Macao Special Administrative Region, except that the restrictions on jurisdiction previously existing in the legal system and principles of Macao shall continue to be maintained. The courts of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall have no jurisdiction over acts of state such as national defense and foreign affairs. When the courts of the Macao Special Administrative Region encounter factual questions involving acts of state such as national defense and foreign affairs during the adjudication of cases, they shall obtain a certification document on such questions from the Chief Executive, which shall be binding on the courts. Before issuing such a certification document, the Chief Executive shall obtain a certificate from the Central People's Government.

Article 20 The Macao Special Administrative Region may enjoy other powers granted to it by the National People's Congress, the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress or the Central People's Government.

Article 21 Chinese citizens who are residents of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall, in accordance with law, participate in the administration of state affairs. In accordance with the number of deputies and the method of their election as determined by the National People's Congress, Chinese citizens who are residents of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall elect, in Macao, the deputies of the Macao Special Administrative Region to the National People's Congress to participate in the work of the highest organ of state power.

Article 22 No department of the Central People's Government, and no province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government may interfere in the affairs which the Macao Special Administrative Region administers on its own in accordance with this Law. If any department of the Central Government, any province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government intends to set up an office in the Macao Special Administrative Region, it shall obtain the consent of the Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region and the approval of the Central People's Government. All offices set up in the Macao Special Administrative Region by any department of the Central Government, any province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, and the personnel thereof, shall abide by the laws of the Macao Special Administrative Region. Persons from provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government entering the Macao Special Administrative Region shall go through the necessary approval procedures. The number of persons from such places who settle in the Macao Special Administrative Region shall be determined by the competent department of the Central People's Government after consulting the Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region. The Macao Special Administrative Region may set up an office in Beijing.

Article 23 The Macao Special Administrative Region shall enact laws on its own to prohibit any act of treason, secession, sedition, subversion against the Central People's Government, or theft of state secrets, to prohibit foreign political organizations or bodies from conducting political activities in the Macao Special Administrative Region, and to prohibit political organizations or bodies of the Macao Special Administrative Region from establishing ties with foreign political organizations or bodies.

Article 24 Residents of the Macao Special Administrative Region, referred to as Macao residents, shall include permanent residents and non-permanent residents. Permanent residents of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall be: (1) Chinese citizens born in Macao before or after the establishment of the Macao Special Administrative Region and their children of Chinese nationality born outside Macao; (2) Chinese citizens who have ordinarily resided in Macao for a continuous period of not less than seven years before or after the establishment of the Macao Special Administrative Region and their children of Chinese nationality born outside Macao after they have become permanent residents; (3) Portuguese who were born in Macao before or after the establishment of the Macao Special Administrative Region and who have taken Macao as their permanent place of residence; (4) Portuguese who have ordinarily resided in Macao for a continuous period of not less than seven years before or after the establishment of the Macao Special Administrative Region and who have taken Macao as their permanent place of residence; (5) Other persons who have ordinarily resided in Macao for a continuous period of not less than seven years before or after the establishment of the Macao Special Administrative Region and who have taken Macao as their permanent place of residence; (6) Children under the age of 18 born in Macao before or after the establishment of the Macao Special Administrative Region of the permanent residents referred to in item (5). The above-mentioned residents shall have the right of abode in the Macao Special Administrative Region and shall be eligible for permanent identity cards of the Macao Special Administrative Region. Non-permanent residents of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall be persons who are eligible for identity cards of the Macao Special Administrative Region in accordance with the laws of the Macao Special Administrative Region but who have no right of abode.

Article 25 All Macao residents shall be equal before the law, and shall not be discriminated against on the grounds of nationality, descent, race, sex, language, religion, political or ideological belief, educational level, economic status, or social condition.
Article 26 Permanent residents of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall have the right to vote and the right to stand for election in accordance with law.

Article 27 Macao residents shall enjoy the freedoms of speech, press, and publication; the freedoms of association, assembly, procession, and demonstration; and the right and freedom to form and join trade unions and to strike.

Article 28 The freedom of the person of Macao residents shall be inviolable. No Macao resident shall be subjected to arbitrary or unlawful arrest, detention, or imprisonment. A resident shall have the right to apply to a court for the issuance of a writ of habeas corpus against arbitrary or unlawful detention or imprisonment. Unlawful search of the body of any resident, or deprivation or restriction of the personal freedom of any resident, shall be prohibited. Torture or inhuman treatment of any resident shall be prohibited.

Article 29 No Macao resident shall be subject to any criminal penalty unless his actions constitute a crime under the law at the time of their commission and are expressly punishable. Macao residents shall have the right to receive a prompt trial in court when charged with a criminal offence and shall be presumed innocent until convicted by a court.

Article 30 The human dignity of Macao residents shall be inviolable. Insult, defamation, and false accusation directed against any resident by any means shall be prohibited. Macao residents shall enjoy the right to personal reputation and the right to privacy of their private and family life.
Article 31 The homes and other premises of Macao residents shall be inviolable. Arbitrary or unlawful search of, or intrusion into, the homes or other premises of residents shall be prohibited.

Article 32 The freedom and confidentiality of communication of Macao residents shall be protected by law. No department or individual may, on any grounds, infringe upon the freedom and confidentiality of communication of residents except that the relevant authorities may inspect communications in accordance with the provisions of law to meet the needs of public security or of investigation into criminal offences.

Article 33 Macao residents shall have the freedom to move within the Macao Special Administrative Region and the freedom to emigrate to other countries and regions. Macao residents shall have the freedom to travel and to enter and leave the Region, and the right to obtain various travel documents in accordance with law. Holders of valid travel documents may leave the Macao Special Administrative Region freely without special authorization, unless restrained by law.

Article 34 Macao residents shall have the freedom of conscience. Macao residents shall have the freedom of religious belief and the freedom to preach and to conduct and participate in religious activities in public.
Article 35 Macao residents shall have the freedom to choose their occupations and jobs.

Article 36 Macao residents shall have the right to have access to the law, to institute legal proceedings in the courts, to obtain the assistance of lawyers for the protection of their lawful rights and interests, and to obtain judicial remedies. Macao residents shall have the right to institute legal proceedings in the courts against the acts of the executive departments and their personnel.
Article 37 Macao residents shall have the freedom to engage in education, academic research, literary and artistic creation, and other cultural activities.

Article 38 The freedom of marriage, the right to establish a family, and the right of voluntary childbearing of Macao residents shall be protected by law. The lawful rights and interests of women shall be protected by the Macao Special Administrative Region. Minors, the elderly, and the disabled shall be cared for and protected by the Macao Special Administrative Region.
Article 39 Macao residents shall have the right to enjoy social welfare in accordance with law. The welfare benefits and retirement security of workers shall be protected by law.

Article 40 The provisions of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, and the international labor conventions as applicable to Macao shall remain in force and shall be implemented through the laws of the Macao Special Administrative Region. The rights and freedoms enjoyed by Macao residents shall not be restricted except as provided for by law. Such restrictions shall not contravene the provisions of the first paragraph of this Article.
Article 41 Residents of Macao shall enjoy other rights and freedoms guaranteed by the laws of the Macao Special Administrative Region.

Article 42 The interests of residents of Portuguese descent in Macao shall be protected by the Macao Special Administrative Region in accordance with law, and their customs and cultural traditions shall be respected.

Article 43 Persons other than residents of Macao who are within the territory of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall, in accordance with law, enjoy the rights and freedoms of residents of Macao provided for in this Chapter.
Article 44 Residents of Macao and other persons in Macao shall have the obligation to abide by the laws in force in the Macao Special Administrative Region.

Article 103 The Macao Special Administrative Region shall, in accordance with law, protect the right of individuals and legal persons to the acquisition, use, disposal and inheritance of property and their right to compensation when their property is expropriated in accordance with law. Such compensation shall correspond to the real value of the property concerned at the time, shall be freely convertible and shall be paid without undue delay. The ownership of enterprises and the investments from outside the Region shall be protected by law.

Article 104 The Macao Special Administrative Region shall maintain independent finances. All revenues of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall be managed and controlled by the Region itself and shall not be turned over to the Central People's Government. The Central People's Government shall not levy taxes in the Macao Special Administrative Region.

Article 105 The budgets of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall be formulated on the principle of keeping expenditure within the limits of revenues, striving to achieve a fiscal balance, avoiding deficits and being commensurate with the growth rate of its gross domestic product.

Article 106 The Macao Special Administrative Region shall adopt an independent taxation system. The Macao Special Administrative Region shall, taking the low tax policy previously in force in Macao as reference, enact laws on its own concerning the types of taxes, tax rates, tax reductions, allowances and exemptions, and other matters of taxation. A franchise tax system shall be otherwise provided by law.

Article 107 The monetary and financial systems of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall be prescribed by law. The Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall, on its own, formulate monetary and financial policies, safeguard the freedom of operation of the financial market and all types of financial institutions, and exercise management and supervision thereof in accordance with law.

Article 108 The Macao Pataca shall be the legal tender in the Macao Special Administrative Region and shall continue to circulate. The authority to issue the Macao currency shall be vested in the Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region. The issue of the Macao currency shall be backed by a 100 per cent reserve fund. The system for the issue of the Macao currency and the reserve fund system shall be prescribed by law. The Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region may authorize designated banks to exercise or continue to exercise the agency function of issuing the Macao currency.

Article 109 The Macao Special Administrative Region shall not impose foreign exchange control policies. The Macao Pataca shall be freely convertible. The foreign exchange reserve of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall be managed and controlled by the Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region in accordance with law. The Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall safeguard the free flow of capital and its entry into and exit from the Region.
Article 110 The Macao Special Administrative Region shall maintain the status of a free port and shall not impose any tariff unless otherwise prescribed by law.
Article 111 The Macao Special Administrative Region shall pursue a policy of free trade and shall safeguard the free flow of goods, intangible assets and capital.

Article 112 The Macao Special Administrative Region shall be a separate customs territory. The Macao Special Administrative Region may, using the name “Macao, China”, participate in relevant international organizations and international trade agreements, including preferential trade arrangements, such as the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade and arrangements regarding international trade in textiles. Export quotas, tariff preferences and other similar arrangements obtained by the Macao Special Administrative Region or obtained previously and still valid shall be enjoyed exclusively by the Region.
Article 113 The Macao Special Administrative Region may issue certificates of origin for products in accordance with the prevailing rules of origin.

Article 114 The Macao Special Administrative Region shall, in accordance with law, protect the freedom of operation of industrial and commercial enterprises and shall, on its own, formulate policies for the development of industry and commerce. The Macao Special Administrative Region shall improve the economic environment and provide legal guarantees to promote the development of industry and commerce, encourage investment and technological progress, and develop new industries and new markets.

Article 115 The Macao Special Administrative Region shall, in light of the economic development of the Region, formulate its own labour policies and improve labour legislation on its own. The Macao Special Administrative Region shall establish a coordinating body of a consultative nature composed of representatives of the government, employers' organizations and employees' organizations.

Article 116 The Macao Special Administrative Region shall maintain and improve the shipping operation and management system previously in force in Macao and shall, on its own, formulate shipping policies. The Macao Special Administrative Region may, with authorization from the Central People's Government, register vessels and, in accordance with the laws of the Macao Special Administrative Region, issue relevant certificates using the name “Macao, China”. Vessels other than foreign military vessels may enter and leave the ports of the Macao Special Administrative Region in accordance with the laws of the Region, provided that the entry of foreign military vessels into the Macao Special Administrative Region shall require the special permission of the Central People's Government. Privately owned shipping enterprises and shipping-related enterprises and terminals in the Macao Special Administrative Region may continue to operate freely.

Article 117 The Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region may, with specific authorization from the Central People's Government, formulate on its own various systems for the administration of civil aviation.
Article 118 The Macao Special Administrative Region shall, on its own, formulate policies on tourism and recreation in light of the overall interests of the Region.
Article 119. The Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall, in accordance with law, protect the environment.

Article 120. The Macao Special Administrative Region shall, in accordance with law, recognize and protect the lawful land leases and all rights relating to such leases which were granted or decided upon before the establishment of the Macao Special Administrative Region and which extend beyond 19 December 1999. Land granted or renewed after the establishment of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall be dealt with in accordance with the relevant land laws and policies of the Macao Special Administrative Region.

Article 121. The Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall formulate its own education policy on its own, including policies on the educational system and its administration, the language of instruction, the allocation of funds, the examination system, the recognition of academic qualifications and degrees, and the like, so as to promote the development of education. The Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall, in accordance with law, implement compulsory education. Community organizations and individuals may, in accordance with law, establish educational undertakings of various kinds.

Article 122. All types of schools originally in Macao may continue to operate. All types of schools in the Macao Special Administrative Region shall have their autonomy in running schools and shall, in accordance with law, enjoy teaching freedom and academic freedom. All types of schools may continue to recruit teaching and administrative staff and use teaching materials from outside the Macao Special Administrative Region. Students shall enjoy the freedom to choose schools and to study outside the Macao Special Administrative Region.

Article 123. The Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall formulate its own policies on its own to promote medical and health services and to develop both Western and traditional Chinese medicine. Community organizations and individuals may, in accordance with law, provide various medical and health services.

Article 124. The Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall formulate its own science and technology policies on its own and shall, in accordance with law, protect scientific and technological research results, patents, and inventions and creations. The Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall determine the scientific and technological standards and specifications applicable to Macao on its own.

Article 125. The Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall formulate its own cultural policies on its own, including policies on literature, art, broadcasting, film, television, and the like. The Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall, in accordance with law, protect the literary, artistic, and other creative achievements and the lawful rights and interests of authors. The Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall, in accordance with law, protect places of scenic beauty, historic sites, and other historical relics and shall protect the lawful rights and interests of their owners.
Article 126. The Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall formulate its own press and publishing policies on its own.

Article 127. The Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall formulate its own sports policies on its own. Non-governmental sports organizations may continue to exist and develop in accordance with law.

Article 128. The Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall, in accordance with the principle of freedom of religious belief, not intervene in the internal affairs of religious organizations, not intervene in the maintenance and development of relations between religious organizations and believers of Macao and their counterparts outside Macao, and not restrict religious activities that do not contravene the laws of the Macao Special Administrative Region. Religious organizations may, in accordance with law, establish seminaries and other schools, hospitals, and welfare institutions, and provide other social services. Schools established by religious organizations may continue to provide religious education, including offering religious courses. Religious organizations shall, in accordance with law, enjoy the right to acquire, use, dispose of, inherit, and receive donations of property. The original rights and interests of religious organizations in property shall be protected in accordance with law.

Article 129. The Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall determine the system of professions on its own. On the basis of the principles of fairness and reasonableness, it shall formulate methods for assessing and conferring various professional and practicing qualifications. Persons who have obtained professional and practicing qualifications prior to the establishment of the Macao Special Administrative Region may retain their original qualifications in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Macao Special Administrative Region. The Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions, recognize the professions and professional organizations that have been recognized prior to the establishment of the Macao Special Administrative Region, and may, in light of the needs of social development and after consulting the views of relevant parties, recognize new professions and professional organizations.

Article 130. On the basis of the original social welfare system, the Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall formulate its own policies on the development and improvement of social welfare on its own, in light of economic conditions and social needs.
Article 131. Social service organizations in the Macao Special Administrative Region may, in the absence of any contravention of the law, decide their own mode of service on their own.

Article 132. The Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall, in light of needs and possibilities, gradually improve the policies previously in force in Macao regarding the funding of non-governmental organizations in such areas as education, science, technology, culture, sports, recreation, medical and health services, social welfare, and social work.

Article 133. The relationship between non-governmental organizations and religious organizations in the Macao Special Administrative Region in such areas as education, science, technology, culture, news, publishing, sports, recreation, professions, medical and health services, labor, women, youth, returned overseas Chinese, social welfare, and social work and their counterparts in other parts of the country shall be based on the principles of non-subordination, non-interference, and mutual respect.

Article 134. Non-governmental organizations and religious organizations in the Macao Special Administrative Region in such areas as education, science, technology, culture, news, publishing, sports, recreation, professions, medical and health services, labor, women, youth, returned overseas Chinese, social welfare, and social work may maintain and develop relations with their counterparts in other countries, regions, and relevant international organizations. Such organizations and groups may, as needed, use the name "Macao, China" in participating in relevant activities.

Article 135. Representatives of the Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region may, as members of the delegation of the Government of the People's Republic of China, participate in diplomatic negotiations conducted by the Central People's Government that are directly related to the Macao Special Administrative Region.

Article 136. The Macao Special Administrative Region may, in appropriate fields such as the economy, trade, finance, shipping, communications, tourism, culture, science and technology, and sports, independently maintain and develop relations with other countries, regions, and relevant international organizations, and conclude and implement relevant agreements, using the name "Macao, China."

Article 137. With respect to international organizations and international conferences to which states are parties and which are relevant to the Macao Special Administrative Region in appropriate fields, the Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region may send representatives to participate as members of the delegation of the People's Republic of China or in such other capacity as may be permitted by the Central People's Government and the relevant international organizations or international conferences, and may express their views using the name "Macao, China." The Macao Special Administrative Region may participate in international organizations and international conferences that are not limited to states using the name "Macao, China." With respect to international organizations in which the People's Republic of China participates and in which Macao also participates in some form, the Central People's Government shall, taking into account circumstances and the needs of the Macao Special Administrative Region, take measures to ensure that the Macao Special Administrative Region continues to maintain its status in such organizations in an appropriate form. With respect to international organizations in which the People's Republic of China has not yet participated but in which Macao has participated in some form, the Central People's Government shall, taking into account circumstances and needs, enable the Macao Special Administrative Region to continue to participate in such organizations in an appropriate form.

Article 138. With respect to international agreements concluded by the People's Republic of China, the Central People's Government may, taking into account circumstances and the needs of the Macao Special Administrative Region, after soliciting the views of the Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region, decide whether they shall apply to the Macao Special Administrative Region. International agreements to which the People's Republic of China is not yet a party but which are already applicable to Macao may continue to apply. The Central People's Government shall, taking into account circumstances and needs, authorize or assist the Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region to make appropriate arrangements for the application to the Macao Special Administrative Region of other relevant international agreements.
